system_description.narrative_title: A Fractured, Tech‑Fueled International Order in Motion
system_description.narrative_summary: The global system is being reshaped by the intersection of an AI-finance cycle, renewed energy‑security shocks from the Middle East, and platform-enabled operational frictions in active conflicts (notably Ukraine). These forces are amplifying sovereign debt and bond-market stress in the Eurozone, accelerating geopolitical competition (US‑China‑Russia) around technology and supply chains, and feeding domestic political instability across advanced democracies. The result is an open, tightly coupled system where financial, technological and kinetic risks propagate rapidly and unpredictably.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and their militaries, international organisations, global energy and commodity markets, sovereign and corporate bond markets, major technology platforms and AI infrastructure, global supply chains, financial institutions, non-state violent actors, and mass public opinion/protest movements.
system_description.super_system: The globalised international political-economic-technical order (the integrated post‑Cold War/21st‑century system of states, markets, and transnational digital infrastructure).

variables.name: US–Iran regional confrontation
variables.description: The escalating confrontation between the United States and Iran — including Iranian proxy strikes, threats to undersea cables and attacks on shipping — is shifting regional deterrence and tying global energy security and oil prices to Middle East escalation risk.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and attrition diplomacy
variables.description: The ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine, sustained by Western military, intelligence and diplomatic backing amid intermittent ceasefires and talks, is changing battlefield dynamics, prompting cyber and infrastructure sabotage and testing the durability of NATO and Western support.

variables.name: US–China technology and supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: The strategic competition between the United States and China over semiconductors, AI, investment controls and influence around Taiwan is reshaping global tech supply chains, export‑control regimes and industrial policy levers.

variables.name: AI build‑out, corporate power and systemic risk
variables.description: A rapid AI infrastructure and chip build‑out led by major tech firms and financed by investors and governments is concentrating corporate power while creating financial, operational and cyber‑security stresses that force new regulatory and fiscal trade‑offs.

variables.name: Eurozone sovereign stress and market fragmentation
variables.description: France's political unrest and rising sovereign yields amid fragile eurozone debt linkages are fragmenting bond markets and compelling the ECB, investors and governments to reassess sovereign risk, monetary policy and fiscal backstops.
